thesis.thesis: Tesla's current fundamentals are dominated by headwinds: robotaxi commercialization is operationally insignificant and contracting, FSD faces active regulatory and legal risk, energy storage growth is being pressured by tariffs before the LG mitigation arrives, executive departures signal organizational instability, and the new vehicle pipeline lacks confirmed consumer deliveries. The bull case relies on early unsupervised rides and a future battery deal, but the evidence does not yet support a growth inflection.

debate.bear: The active unsupervised fleet is only ~20 vehicles and shrinking, Q2 2026 paid miles fell 36% QoQ while Waymo clears ~4 million miles a week, and 245 Cybercabs sit parked with no paying passengers—so Tesla is not closing the gap and has no meaningful robotaxi revenue in sight.

debate.verdict: The bear wins: unsupervised rides and geofence expansion are real but the fleet is tiny, shrinking, and paid miles are falling, while Waymo is 24–36 months ahead. Cybercab production capacity is idle, so scaling is not happening.

debate.bull: Tesla's ADS incident count (18) is far below Waymo's (~697), and FSD software updates can address the specific traffic-rule violations; NHTSA probes may end with limited recalls rather than restrictions on unsupervised deployment.

debate.verdict: The bear wins: the volume of documented violations, multiple open probes, and an adverse wrongful death verdict are concrete legal and regulatory headwinds; the bull's lower incident count is not comparable because Tesla's robotaxi fleet is barely operating.

debate.verdict: The bear narrowly wins: the LG deal is a real mitigation but starts in 2027, while current 54% tariffs and CFO warnings create immediate margin pressure on the one growing segment.

debate.bull: Executive departures are normal churn after rapid growth, and Tesla's vertical integration, brand loyalty, and AI/robotics mission still attract top engineering talent, as institutional investors acknowledge.

debate.bear: Tesla has lost its 10th executive in 2025, including the heads of Cybertruck, Optimus, battery architecture, and North America/Europe operations—this is not normal churn but a sign of organizational instability that can delay Cybercab, Model 2, and Optimus.

bear_source.title: What’s Going On at Tesla? A Wave of Executives Is Heading for the Exits

debate.verdict: The bear wins: the breadth and seniority of departures—10+ executives across core programs—overwhelms the generic argument that churn is normal, and there is no evidence of successful retention or replacement.

debate.bull: Tesla has begun Cybercab pilot production and delivered 2,500 pilot units of the affordable Model 2 to European fleet operators in early 2026, with mass consumer deliveries targeted for late 2026—concrete execution on the new vehicle pipeline.

bull_source.title: Tesla Model 2 Comeback: Bringing Back Its Affordable EV

debate.bear: No affordable model is confirmed for consumer delivery, the Roadster is 12–18 months from production at best, and Tesla remains dependent on aging Model 3/Y while competitors gain share—pilot units to fleets are not consumer sales.

bear_source.title: Tesla future models: Roadster and affordable EV status

debate.verdict: The bear narrowly wins: pilot production and fleet deliveries are progress, but the key $25,000 consumer vehicle is still unconfirmed, Roadster is far off, and the volume growth thesis depends on execution that has repeatedly slipped.

falsifiers: Robotaxi paid miles return to sequential growth and active unsupervised fleet exceeds 100 vehicles in Austin.
NHTSA closes all FSD investigations without a recall or operational restriction and no new wrongful death verdicts.
Energy storage gross margin remains stable or improves in the next two quarters despite 54% tariffs.
Executive departures stop and key vacant roles (Cybertruck, Optimus, battery) are filled with proven leaders.
Tesla confirms and begins consumer deliveries of a sub-$30,000 vehicle before end of 2026.
thesis.confidence_why: All five debated drivers resolved in favor of the bear, with multiple independent sources and concrete metrics (paid miles, NHTSA case numbers, executive departures, tariff rates) supporting the headwinds. The bull evidence is real but early-stage or future-dated, and does not offset current operational and regulatory pressure.

catalysts.expected: Beat/raise: rebound in auto margins, record energy storage revenue, and progress on robotaxi/Cybercab could restore growth narrative and lift shares. Miss/cut: another YoY auto revenue decline, margin compression from tariffs, or weak robotaxi paid-mile growth would intensify bear-case valuation con

catalysts.event: Cybercab pilot production ramp and first paid passenger service
catalysts.expected: Successful ramp: VIN/production growth accelerates, vehicles carry paying passengers, and Tesla narrows the perceived gap with Waymo, supporting the AI/robotaxi premium. Delay/stall: inventory piles at Gigaf Texas, no commercial paid rides, and fleet stays tiny, undermining the core bull thesis.

catalysts.event: Model 2 / Project Redwood mass consumer deliveries
catalysts.expected: On-time and priced near $25k: adds volume, stabilizes automotive revenue, and improves investor confidence after executive turnover. Delay or limited rollout: further auto revenue erosion and pressure on growth multiples.

Compelling demo and clear production timeline: generates brand buzz, deposits/orders, and distracts from weak core auto trends. Underwhelming demo or further delay: reinforces product-pipeline skepticism and weighs on sentiment.

catalysts.event: NHTSA FSD/Autopilot investigation outcomes (PE25012, AQ25002, PE24031)
catalysts.expected: No formal recall or limited remedy: allows FSD subscription/revenue growth and robotaxi expansion to continue with modest overhang. Recall, enforcement, or expanded probe: raises compliance costs, limits rollout, damages brand, and creates liability headwinds.

catalysts.event: Tesla Robotaxi unsupervised scaling in Texas and new markets
catalysts.expected: Fleet materially expands, safety drivers are removed, and fares/volume rise: validates Tesla's camera-only approach and re-rates the stock toward AI/robotics. Fleet stays ~20-50 vehicles, supervised rides persist, and paid miles fall: confirms Waymo's 24-36 month lead and erodes the robotaxi narrati

catalysts.event: LG Energy Solution Michigan LFP battery supply for Megapack 3
catalysts.expected: On schedule: shifts Megapack cell sourcing out of China, mitigating 54% tariff exposure and protecting energy margins. Delay or qualification issues: energy storage costs rise, Powerwall/Megapack pricing power erodes, and the fast-growing segment faces margin pressure.

catalysts.event: Hertz disposition of Tesla/EV fleet and residual-value impact
catalysts.expected: Faster sales completion: removes used-Tesla oversupply and stabilizes resale values. Continued fire sales / large write-downs: depresses used Tesla prices, hurts Tesla's new-car pricing power and finance/lease residuals.
